records.text: In the fifteenth year of Amaziah son of Joash, king of Judah, Jeroboam son of Joash became king over Israel in Samaria, for forty-one years.
He did evil before the Lord. He did not turn away from any of the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.

He shifted Israel’s boundary from the entrance of Aimath to the Sea of the Arabah, according to the word of the Lord, Israel’s God, which He spoke through His servant Jonah son of Amathi, the prophet from Gethchober.
For the Lord saw Israel’s humiliation was very bitter, and they were few, hemmed in, impoverished, and abandoned; there was no one helping Israel.
The Lord had not spoken of blotting out Israel’s seed from beneath heaven, and He saved them through Jeroboam son of Joash.
Where can I go from Thy Spirit, and where can I flee from Thy face?
If I ascend to heaven, Thou art there; if I descend into Hades, Thou art present.
if I take up my wings at dawn and settle at the sea’s farthest reaches,
indeed, even there Thy hand will guide me, and Thy right hand will hold me fast.
And I said, “Then darkness will trample me, and night is light in my delight.”
For darkness will not be dark from Thee, and night will be lit up like day; as its darkness, so also its light.
On that day, when evening came, He said to them, “Let us cross to the other side.”
Leaving the crowd, they took Him with them, just as He was, in the boat. Other boats were with Him.
A great windstorm arose, and the waves broke into the boat, so that the boat was already filling.
He was in the stern, asleep on the cushion. They woke Him and said to Him, “Teacher, dost Thou not care that we are perishing?”
And He awoke, rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, “Be silent; be still.” And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.
He said to them, “Why are you cowardly? Do you still have no faith?”
They were greatly afraid and said to one another, “Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey Him?”
Those going down into the sea in ships, doing work on many waters,
they saw the Lord’s works and His wonders in the depth.
He spoke, and a storm wind stood, and its waves were raised.
They rise as far as the heavens and descend as far as the deeps; their soul melted in evils.
They were troubled and shaken like a drunken man, and all their wisdom was swallowed up.
They cried to the Lord when they were afflicted, and He brought them out of their distresses,
and commanded the storm, and it settled into a breeze, and its waves fell silent.
They rejoiced because they became quiet, and He guided them to the harbor of their desire.
Let them acknowledge to the Lord His mercies and His wonders to the sons of men,
let them exalt Him in an assembly of the people and praise Him where the elders sit.
As we were violently battered by the storm, the next day they began throwing cargo overboard.
On the third day they threw the ship’s tackle overboard with their own hands.
When neither sun nor stars appeared for many days, and a fierce storm kept battering us, all remaining hope of our being saved was taken away.
For in six days the Lord made heaven and earth and the sea and everything in them, and rested on the seventh day. Therefore the Lord blessed the seventh day and made it holy.

Arise, consecrate the people, and tell them to consecrate themselves for tomorrow. Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: ‘What is under the ban is among you. You cannot withstand your enemies until you remove it from among you.’

In the morning you shall all assemble by tribes. Bring forward by clans the tribe which the Lord indicates; bring forward by households the clan which the Lord indicates; and bring forward man by man the household which the Lord indicates.
Whoever is indicated shall be burned with fire, together with everything belonging to him, because he transgressed the Lord’s covenant and committed lawlessness in Israel.”
Joshua rose early and brought the people forward by tribes. The tribe of Judah was indicated.
They were brought forward by clans, and the Zerahite clan was indicated. They were brought forward man by man,
and Achar son of Zambri, son of Zerah, was indicated.
Joshua said to Achar, “Give glory today to the Lord, the God of Israel, and make confession. Tell me what you have done, and do not hide it from me.”
Achar answered Joshua, “Truly I have sinned before the Lord, the God of Israel. This is what I did:
and shall answer and say: Our hands have not shed this blood, neither have our eyes seen it.

Be merciful unto Thy people Israel, whom Thou hast redeemed, O Lord, out of the land of Egypt, that there be no guilt of innocent blood among Thy people Israel. And atonement shall be made for the blood on their behalf.
And you shall remove the guilt of innocent blood from among yourselves, if you do that which is good and pleasing before the Lord your God.
